questions.question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Followed
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"followed"** means to come after in sequence or time, to go or come after, or to act according to (a law or instruction). (अनुसरण किया)

 
 
• **Example:** She followed the instructions carefully to complete the project.
 
 
 
• **"Obeyed"** refers to complying with a command, order, or law; to follow the directions or instructions of someone. (आज्ञा का पालन किया)
 
 
• **Example:** The soldiers obeyed the general's orders without question.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word that means the same as 'followed' is 'obeyed'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Transgressed** (उल्लंघन किया): To violate a law, command, or moral code.

 
 
• **Example:** He transgressed the rules by cheating in the exam.
 
 
 
• **Claimed** (दावा किया): To assert or demand recognition of (a right, title, possession, etc.); to state as a fact.
 
 
• **Example:** She claimed that the book was hers.
 
 
 
• **Disobliged** (नाराज किया): To refuse or neglect to do something; to cause inconvenience or discomfort.
 
 
• **Example:** He disobliged his friends by not attending the party.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom / Phrase.

To sit at someone's feet

options.text: To attend upon as someone's disciple

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To attend upon as someone's disciple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To sit at someone's feet"** means to be a devoted follower or disciple of someone, often a mentor or a teacher. (किसी के शिष्य बनना)

 
 
• **Example: **Many young musicians wish to sit at the feet of a great master like Ravi Shankar to learn the intricacies of classical music.
 
 
 
• **To attend upon as someone's disciple** implies being a dedicated student or follower who learns and respects the teachings of a mentor. (किसी के शिष्य के रूप में उपस्थित होना)
 
 
• **Example: **He spent years attending upon the feet of his guru, absorbing every lesson and wisdom imparted.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To attend upon as someone's disciple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To wash someone's feet **(किसी के पैर धोना): Literally means to clean someone's feet, often as a sign of respect or servitude.

 
 
• **Example:** In many cultures, washing someone's feet is a sign of humility and respect.
 
 
 
• **To be someone's equal **(किसी के बराबर होना ): To be on the same level in terms of status, ability, or rank.
 
 
• **Example: **Despite his young age, he proved to be his mentor's equal in terms of skill and knowledge.
 
 
 
• **To be proud of someone** (किसी पर गर्व करना): To feel pride due to someone's achievements or qualities.
 
 
• **Example:** She is very proud of her son's accomplishments in the field of medicine.
